definitions.explanation: A sweeping, fundamental change to a system, institution, or way of doing things. Stronger than mere improvement — implies restructuring or overhaul at a deep level.

examples.japanese: {社会|しゃかい}{変革|へんかく}を{目指|めざ}す。
{技術|ぎじゅつ}の{進歩|しんぽ}が{産業|さんぎょう}に{大|おお}きな{変革|へんかく}をもたらした。
examples.english: Technological progress brought about great transformation in industry.

examples.japanese: {教育|きょういく}{制度|せいど}の{変革|へんかく}なくして、この{問題|もんだい}は{解決|かいけつ}しないだろう。
examples.english: Without reform of the education system, this problem will likely not be solved.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal word used in political, social, and business contexts. Often appears in discussions of systemic or institutional change. Carries a more dramatic, fundamental connotation than {改革|かいかく} (reform), though the two overlap significantly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {社会|しゃかい}{変革|へんかく}: social reform/revolution
- {意識|いしき}{変革|へんかく}: change in mindset
- {変革|へんかく}を{起|お}こす: bring about change
- {変革|へんかく}の{時代|じだい}: era of transformation
- {構造|こうぞう}{変革|へんかく}: structural transformation

SIMILAR WORDS:
{変革|へんかく} implies a fundamental, sweeping transformation. {改革|かいかく} (reform) is the most common word for institutional reform and may be more incremental. {革命|かくめい} (revolution) implies even more drastic, often violent change.
